newsitem.title: USA: Intel cuts Pentium prices up to 57 percent.
newsitem.headline: Intel cuts Pentium prices up to 57 percent.

text.p: Intel Corp., as expected, Monday slashed prices of its Pentium microprocessors by up to 57 percent, which will mean lower personal computer prices in coming months.
The world's biggest computer chip maker said Monday it cut the price of the top-of-the-line Pentium II 300 MHz chip -- currently used primarily in engineering workstations -- by 57 percent to $851.
The price of the Pentium 233 MHz with MMX chip -- one of the most popular models for home and multimedia PCs -- was slashed 35 percent to $386.

Intel cuts prices of its chips about once a quarter. Since more than 80 percent of the world's personal computers use Intel chips, the summer price cuts determine PC prices during the crucial back-to-school shopping season.

Analysts have said this summer's price cuts are steeper than usual. Intel wants to move out its older generation of Pentium chips and wants to make its Pentium II chips more affordable to regular PC users.
"The new prices reflect Intel's continued delivery of increased performance at each price point," the company said in a statement.
The prices became effective for PC makers Sunday, but were officially announced Monday.
Intel stock slipped 69 cents to $88.50 in afternoon trading on Nasdaq.
